items.title: Lawrence Duhé Interview, 1960
items.q: Yeah, Bunk and I joined the Banner Band about the same time when Bunk came from New Orleans to join the Banner Band.

ctx.x: What year was this? Well, all right. He doesn't know. Mr. Dewey, would you tell us about your coming back south, about what time you came back here and your reasons for coming back south?

For coming back south, I got in bad health up to Cunningham, and the doctor had ordered me to stop playing. So I came to New Orleans to rest up. while there, after I rest up for a while, Jack Carey asked me to come out to Lafayette to play a dollar excursion as one of the men had taken sick. So I came out here to Lafayette to play a one Sunday dollar excursion, and I've been around Lafayette since. Mr. Dewey, would you explain to Forest students who are young and don't know what is a dollar excursion? A dollar…

items.title: Lawrence Duhé Interview, 1957-06-09
items.q: Not when I first joined, but after I was in there, well, I got him.

ctx.x: When do you think, how long you started there in 1921 or so maybe then? I guess so around the 20s, yeah. When was Bunk in it then, when you joined?

Not when I first joined, but after I was in there, well, I got him. You don't know just 20 joined then? No, I don't know when. I used to go to New Orleans and get substitutes, you know, with plays, just like I did in the Black Eagle. Black Eagle, I went and got Earl Humphrey and John Joseph, Irvin Joseph on drum. Irvin, that's my cousin. Yeah, Tom Benton.
Oh, he had banjo or guitarist. Yeah, well, I got reinforced those country bands. I was bunking the Black Eagle band too for a while. Yeah, uh-huh. With you, same time as you? No, not same time.
